anomaly_def.Name: Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Composite anomaly definition: The database concurrently experiences on-disk data/index corruption, sustained saturation of the underlying storage devices, and near-maximum consumption of host CPU resources. The coexistence of these three root causes causes intertwined integrity faults, I/O bottlenecks, and compute starvation that jointly threaten both correctness and performance across transactional and analytical workloads.

Combined anomalous phenomena: Operators that rely on indexes intermittently miss or duplicate rows while their response times swing unpredictably; repeated checksum failures, page-repair attempts, and forced re-reads inflate read amplification and drive I/O queues to their limits, causing device latencies to spike into seconds. Simultaneously, database worker threads spin on retries and error handling, pushing CPU utilization to 100 %, swelling run queues, and surfacing scheduler and I/O wait events side-by-side. Batch jobs overrun maintenance windows, OLTP transactions time out or deadlock on corrupted pages, recovery processes loop, and monitoring shows a mixture of physical corruption alerts, persistent PAGEIOLATCH/IO_COMPLETION waits, and high CPU_TIME rankings for error-handling routines.

Causal interaction: Corrupted data or index pages force the engine to issue repeated physical reads, trigger consistency checks, and invoke page-repair or rebuild tasks, all of which amplify demand on an already saturated storage subsystem. The heightened I/O contention elongates each access, causing worker threads to block and then surge when I/O completes, which in turn spikes CPU consumption through excessive context switching, spin-locks, and retry logic. Conversely, CPU saturation slows background tasks such as checksum validation, buffer flushing, and recovery, prolonging the window during which corrupted pages remain in circulation. The prolonged I/O queues also increase the chance of further write interruptions or incomplete flushes, potentially deepening the underlying corruption. The feedback loop among corruption handling, storage overload, and CPU exhaustion drives the database into a degraded and unstable state where both performance and data integrity are simultaneously compromised.

entry.official_definition: Maximum wait for connection, in seconds; zero or not specified means wait indefinitely.
entry.trigger_condition: A libpq client connection attempt exceeds connect_timeout seconds.
entry.workload_impact: The client connection attempt fails instead of waiting indefinitely.
entry.default_behavior: Zero or absent value means wait indefinitely.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
